linkedin.title: We decided to make our news feed less efficient on purpose.
linkedin.body:
Most news apps are built to maximize engagement at all costs. Their algorithms are designed to show you things that keep you scrolling for as long as possible. We took a different path with Headlinne.

We intentionally introduced a bit of friction into our recommendation engine. Instead of just feeding you more of what you already like, we occasionally surface topics that challenge your existing perspective or simply offer a different angle on the same event. It makes the feed feel slightly less like a comfortable echo chamber and more like a conversation.

This is a harder engineering challenge because it means we cannot rely on simple engagement metrics to measure success. It requires us to prioritize quality and diversity over pure screen time. We believe that if you want to stay informed, you need to see the full picture, not just the parts that make you nod along.

Building software that respects your attention span is a constant balancing act. But we think it is the only way to build a product that actually helps you understand the world better.

slides.subtitle: President threatens tremendous penalties for building infrastructure abroad

slides.explanation: While no specific penalty amount was announced, these facilities often cost billions of dollars to build and power, making them massive infrastructure projects.

slides.headline: He has not yet informed the companies involved
slides.explanation: Despite the public threat of penalties, the President acknowledged he has not actually spoken to the tech firms about this plan yet.
Six independent news outlets, including The Verge and NPR, confirm these remarks were made during a recent White House press conference.

instagram.caption:
President Trump recently signaled a major shift for the tech industry, stating he plans to penalize American companies that

move their datacenter operations outside of the United States.  He framed this as a way to keep infrastructure domestic, though he did not provide specific details on what those penalties would look like or how they would be enforced.  Interestingly, the President also noted he has not yet spoken with the executives of the companies this policy would impact.
